phases.name: Spring Boot 4.1, bootstrap and enforcement foundation

steps.name: Upgrade to Spring Boot 4.1 with walking skeleton green
criteria: ./mvnw verify passes on Spring Boot 4.1 with the walking skeleton green, including its check that no file or folder name is sent to Jev.
ApplicationDefaultsContractTest's key and log guard stays green.
Static gate (pom.xml review, Maven Central lookup): exact Boot 4.1 patch pinned; Cucumber, WireMock, ArchUnit and PIT versions verified against its JUnit and recorded.
Static gate (grep of src for com.fasterxml.jackson.databind): no project code, main or test, uses Jackson 2 databind; reports keep their JSON content.
Static gate (grep of application.yml): no spring.http.client key remains; Jev limits (10 s, 30 s) come from detector.jev settings.
steps.scenario_name: A good-looking part passes and a part with a cut lead is documented as scrap
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-006, DDD-27, DDD-37, OQ-6. Removing spring.http.client would leave real runs without limits, so the existing adapter applies detector.jev.* until 04-01. WalkingSkeletonSteps: only JSON import and mapper change. Add ArchUnit here; PIT follows in 01-03. The WireMock version also pins the 06-02 image. Fallback: newest compatible versions, pinned. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: Bootstrap launcher, single file ports and first real-jar scenario
criteria: The real jar inspects a folder, prints only the agreed summary line with the output path as typed, reports no problem and exits 0.
A completed batch adds only its declared files, including damage-detector.log, keeps files already in the output folder unchanged and leaves the input tree unchanged.
Only .png, .jpg and .jpeg images, upper or lower case, are inspected; other files in the input are ignored.
report.json and report.md carry the agreed batch fields: jevCost replaces totalCost, plus judged, jevErrors and costIsLowerBound.
Console logging stays off by default and --debug changes no results; the real-jar suite fails when it finds no scenario.

steps.implementation_notes: DDD-28, DDD-30, Q11. LogSink moves here from slice 05: the completed-batch universe requires the log. Happy path only; refusals land in 05-01 and 05-02. Inspector reads through ImageFolder and wraps the old port result as Judged until 04-01. Use cases take folders and PassPolicy per run. ImageFolder and OutputFolder implement Probe. DetectorCommand must run without the bootstrap: the skeleton skips it. Move class-level @Disabled to methods. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: ArchUnit rules, CI workflow and PIT mutation precursor
criteria: Process gate (seeded violation per rule, ./mvnw verify): each active rule fails once on a violation, and any violation fails the build.
Static gate (ArchitectureRulesTest listing): rules 1 to 4, 6, 7 and 8 are active; rule 5 and rule 8's jev-to-root edge stay visibly pending until 04-01.
Static gate (workflow lint): verify and mutation run on pull requests, verify on pushes to main, with read-only permissions, no secrets and SHA-pinned actions.
Static gate (workflow lint): the verify job scans the full git history and fails on a secret; a live run waits for a remote.
Process gate (local PIT run): changed classes are gated at an 80 % kill rate, using JUnit tests only and leaving out the wiring classes.
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-17; DEVOPS CI and mutation sections; item 15. DISTILL wrote no rule tests, so this step writes them. OpenRouterJev keeps implements Jev and its DetectorProperties import until 04-01: keep rule 5 and the edge @Disabled with that reason. No remote exists, so run verify and PIT locally. PIT counts acceptance-only classes as uncovered: list those for the user. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: Evaluate mode scores a labelled folder
criteria: --evaluate on a labelled folder writes evaluation.md, evaluation.json and one summary line with false passes, good auto-pass and defects not passed.
Recall counts images not passed; the correct suspected class is counted separately.
The class table shows every defect class in fixed order, with zero rows for a class without images.
The label is the exact first path segment below the input, however deep the image lies.
A completed evaluation leaves only its two records and the log: no scrap or review copies, and the input is unchanged.
steps.scenario_name: Presenter sees zero false passes on the labelled set | Presenter sees how many good parts pass automatically | Presenter sees the recall of each defect class | A wrong suspected class does not count as correct | An evaluation writes nothing but its declared files | An image in a deeper sub-folder keeps its label | A class without images is still shown, with zero rows | LabelResolutionTest (all methods) | EvaluationTest#a_false_pass_is_a_defect_jev_called_good_at_or_above_the_threshold | EvaluationTest#counts_add_up | CliArgumentsTest#evaluate_alone_selects_the_evaluation
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-3, DDD-13, DDD-14 (field names ratified; sweep fields land in 03-01). Reuse Inspector. A label is resolved only in evaluate/, as a pure function. LabelledEvaluation: orchestration, no direct IO. EvaluationWriter: bounded change through OutputFolder. Until 04-01 a Jev failure aborts the run. Move EvaluationTest's class-level @Disabled to methods. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: False passes, label privacy and labelled-folder refusal
criteria: A defect judged GOOD at or above the threshold is listed with path and P(GOOD); the run prints one stderr line and exits 2.
With threshold 0.86, a defect at P(GOOD) 0.85 is REVIEW and the run exits 0; at exactly 0.86 it is a false pass.
No Jev request carries a file name, relative path, label with separator or input folder name; apart from the image data, requests are identical.
An image without an exact label is counted as skipped and never sent to Jev.
A folder without labelled images gets the line naming the five sub-folders, exit 1, no Jev call and only the log written.
steps.scenario_name: A defect that passes is named as a false pass | A false pass is also reported as a problem | The false-pass line sits exactly at the pass threshold | The class table separates recall from the suspected class | Folder names are only used for scoring | An image without a label is skipped, counted and not sent to Jev | A folder without labels is refused before any cost | ErrorFeedbackTest#a_false_pass_points_to_the_evaluation
steps.implementation_notes: D18, Q7, DDD-13, DDD-24, DDD-33, UC-2, UC-3. First non-zero exits: report them through ExitCodeGenerator. ErrorFeedback stays pure and gains only its exit-2 line and the NO_LABELLED_IMAGES text; the full table lands in 05-01. Move ErrorFeedbackTest's class-level @Disabled to methods. "A defect that passes" runs on the real jar, so exit 2 must reach the process. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: Evaluation evidence, golden response and real 253-image run
criteria: evaluation.md and evaluation.json state the run date, Jev cost and elapsed seconds; evaluation.md adds the SPIKE disclosure and ends with the MVTec AD attribution.
Re-running into the same folder replaces both evaluation records as a whole and leaves other files untouched.
Static gate (file review, grep for the key prefix): src/test/resources/jev/golden-response.json holds one real, unmodified Jev response and no key.
Closing gate (brief entry): the slice-01 brief holds summary line, per-class table, date, cost and time of the full 253-image run, or a user waiver.
Static gate (grep of README.md): it shows the evaluate command and the exit codes 0, 1 and 2.
steps.scenario_name: Evaluation result can be read from the command line | The evaluation keeps its cost and duration as evidence | The evaluation names its run date | The evaluation says what its defect images can and cannot prove | The evaluation names the source of the sample data | Running the evaluation again replaces the earlier record
steps.implementation_notes: D26, K1, K5, OQ-5, item 8. Real calls: load .env with set -a; never print, log or pass the key as an argument. About $0.04, 5 min. Exit 2 is a finding, not a step failure: record it and tell the user. Rerun budget: up to 2 reruns if a Jev failure aborts the run (about $0.04 each). Golden: one raw call on one image, unmodified; its test runs in 04-01. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: Threshold sweep from one Jev pass
criteria: evaluation.json holds a sweep row for every threshold 0.50 to 0.99 plus the configured value; evaluation.md shows 0.80 to 0.95 plus the configured value.
The row of the configured threshold equals the headline numbers, also for an off-grid value such as 0.875.
The evaluation names the lowest threshold with 0 false passes, or says none up to 0.99 exists.
Jev is called once per labelled image whatever the sweep size, and the tool never changes the configured threshold.
Closing gate (brief entry): the slice-02 brief holds summary line, date, cost and sweep of a real 253-image run, plus the user's threshold decision, or a user waiver.

steps.implementation_notes: D17, DDD-4, DDD-14 items 9 and 10, K2. Pure recomputation over stored outcomes, in hundredths. This needs a second paid run (about $0.04): the 02-03 record has no sweep. The threshold decision is the user's: record the evidence and ask; change no default alone. Rerun budget: up to 2 reruns if a Jev failure aborts the run (about $0.04 each). A batch into the same folder must keep the evaluation files. @sizing-review-needed. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: Retry decorator: failed images reach REVIEW, batch continues
criteria: An image failing on every attempt becomes REVIEW with the pinned description, a copy and a .txt, and the remaining images are still inspected.
Transient failures are retried up to the attempt limit; other 4xx end after one attempt; a later success gives the normal verdict and no Jev error.
An unreadable or invalid answer is transient: retried to the attempt limit, then REVIEW with unreadable answer, never a verdict, whatever its P(GOOD).
With 2 of 10 images failing, reports and summary agree (3 PASS, 4 SCRAP, 3 REVIEW, 2 Jev errors, 8 judged); report.json marks each errored image.
The golden test asserts the parsed verdict and P(GOOD) of the recorded answer; ArchUnit rule 5 and the jev-to-root edge are enabled and green.

Remove implements Jev, the DetectorProperties constructor and judge() from OpenRouterJev. Build the client at the first attempt. Until 05-02 no key check exists: a missing key means 401s, then REVIEW. Move RetryingJevTest and RetryingJevAttemptLoopTest class-level @Disabled to methods, keeping later-step methods disabled. @sizing-review-needed. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: Growing waits, Retry-After and cost as lower bound
criteria: Waits between attempts double from the initial backoff and stop at the longest allowed wait; no wait follows the last attempt.
A Retry-After within the limit replaces the backoff, an unusable one is ignored, and one above the limit ends the attempts at once with the pinned reason.
The attempts per image are configurable, and the description states the real count in correct singular or plural.
After any failed attempt, even one followed by a success, batch and evaluation outputs mark the cost as a lower bound.
Without a failed attempt the cost is exact and the words lower bound appear nowhere.

steps.implementation_notes: ADR-004, DDD-6, 7, 15, Q3. The cost of failed attempts is unknown and not counted. In-process scenarios record waits with the fake sleeper; the real sleeper runs in real-jar scenarios with 1 ms waits. Plain doubling may already pass after 04-01: the cap and Retry-After are this step's RED. RetryingJevTest, RetryingJevAttemptLoopTest: lift only this step's method-level @Disabled, keeping later-step methods disabled. @sizing-review-needed. TEST PARADIGM: JUnit @ParameterizedTest example tables and exhaustive finite sets at layer 1; Cucumber scenarios at acceptance; StateDelta universe assertions per DISTILL. Do not add a PBT library.

steps.name: Nothing-judged guard, interrupted runs and atomic reports
criteria: When no image was judged, batch and evaluation still write their reports, print the line naming OPENROUTER_API_KEY and the network, and exit 3.
A run stopped by Ctrl-C or a stop request ends with 130 or 143 and leaves no finished report, only its declared files; exit 137 is a manual check.
Every report appears whole under its final name, the .md record last; a failed replacement keeps the old file and no temp file remains.
The API key appears nowhere in console output, log or reports, with or without --debug.
Closing gate (brief entry): the slice-03 brief holds summary line, date and cost of a 10-image run with ~10 s network loss and ≥1 Jev error, or a user waiver.

steps.implementation_notes: D14, D25, DDD-16, DDD-34, INV-3, INV-6, DEVOPS interrupt contract. No signal handler: the JVM sets the codes. Publish copies and .txt, then the .json, then the .md. Exit 3 outranks 2. Exit 137: manual kill -9 check, because SIGKILL cannot be trapped; record it in the brief. If you cannot cut the network, ask the user for a hand run or waiver. README: exits 3, 130, 143, 137 and the fresh-folder rerun. steps.name: Refuse bad command lines and unusable output before writing
criteria: Missing options, an unknown option or a value after --evaluate give the usage line naming the problem, exit 1, no Jev call and nothing written.
A typo such as --evalute can never start a paid run; dotted properties and the debug and trace flags stay allowed.
An input folder that does not exist or is a file is refused with its path as typed.
An output equal to or inside the input is refused before any write, also through a symlink or .. across missing folders.
An output that is read-only, a file or below a file gets the cannot-write line with its cause, and no log file appears.

steps.name: Half A: Docker image, self-test, key scan, demo commands
criteria: Process gate (docker build, docker image inspect): the image builds with Docker only, runs as a non-root user and accepts the jar's flags.
Process gate (scripts/container-check.sh --self-test): it reports FAIL on a deliberately bad image before any Docker scenario is enabled.
The shared image holds no key, .env or key name in its configuration, history, layers or jar.
Running the check leaves the real .env byte-identical on every exit path and never prints it.
Closing gate (brief entry): the slice-04 brief holds summary line, date and cost of the documented batch command on at least 5 real images, or a user waiver.

criteria: Docker and jar runs on the same stubbed Jev answers give equal verdict counts and the same output files; evaluation works in Docker too.
Docker passes on the run endings: missing key and forgotten output mount 1, all calls rejected 3, false pass 2.

The invoking user can delete everything in the output folder without extra rights.
A rollback to the previous SHA tag runs one fixture, and pull requests and main run the check in the image job.
